name: דוגמה לפונקציה עם נקודה סטציונרית ב-x=n, רציפה ולא גזירה ב-0 (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Give an example of a function \(f(x)\) with a stationary point at \(x={{CT:0}}\) and which is continuous but not differentiable at \(x=0\).

\(f(x)=\) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: There are many correct answers; we build one. A function with a stationary point at \(x={{CT:0}}\) is bent at \(x=0\) with the absolute value \(|x|\), which keeps it continuous but creates a corner.
Step 1 — A quadratic with the right stationary point
The parabola \(x(x-{{CT:1}})\) has roots \(0\) and \({{CT:1}}\); its vertex lies halfway between them, at \(x={{CT:0}}\), so its derivative \({{CT:2}}\) vanishes there.
Step 2 — Bending it at 0
Replace the factor \(x\) by \(|x|\):

\[ f(x)={{CT:3}} \]

For \(x\gt 0\) this is the same parabola \({{CT:4}}\), so \(f'(x)={{CT:2}}\) and \(f'({{CT:0}})=0\): the stationary point is kept.
Step 3 — Continuity and the corner at 0
\(f\) is a product of continuous functions, so it is continuous at \(0\), with \(f(0)=0\). The one-sided derivatives at \(0\) differ:

\[ f'_+(0)=\lim_{h\to 0^+}\frac{h(h-{{CT:1}})}{h}={{CT:5}},\qquad f'_-(0)=\lim_{h\to 0^-}\frac{-h(h-{{CT:1}})}{h}={{CT:1}} \]

so \(f\) is not differentiable at \(0\). One answer is therefore

\[ f(x)={{CT:3}} \]

on_false.feedback: Your answer does not have a stationary point at \(x={{CT:0}}\) but should do.
Your answer is not continuous at \(x=0\), but needs to be.
Your answer is differentiable at \(x=0\) but should not be. Consider using \(|x|\), which is entered as abs(x), somewhere in your answer.
